title: Day 15 — Security: Path Traversal
prompt: This endpoint serves files from a base directory using a user-supplied path. A pen test says you can read /etc/passwd through it. Take a look — how do you lock it down?

clarifications.answer: The attacks are '../' escapes, absolute paths like /etc/passwd, and mid-path tricks like a/../../etc. All must throw.
On an unsafe path, throw Error('unsafe path'). On a safe path, return the resolved absolute path.
Normalization that stays inside is fine: 'reports/../q1.txt' should resolve to baseDir/q1.txt and be allowed.
Careful: a bare startsWith(base) is buggy — '/srv/data-evil' starts with '/srv/data'. Check for base itself OR base + path separator.
path.join normalizes but happily produces paths outside the base (../) and mishandles absolute inputs. You must resolve then verify containment.
Out of scope here — assume no symlinks; just do lexical containment on resolved absolute paths.

hints: path.join isn't a security boundary — it will cheerfully return /srv/secret from '../secret'.
Resolve both to absolute: base = path.resolve(baseDir); candidate = path.resolve(base, userPath). Then check containment.
Allow when candidate === base or candidate.startsWith(base + path.sep); otherwise throw. The separator check defeats the sibling-prefix trick.
